newsitem.title: UK: S&P says may still downgrade Northern Electric.
newsitem.headline: S&P says may still downgrade Northern Electric.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday the A and A1 ratings of Northern Electric would remain on CreditWatch with negative implications pending resolution of a takeover bid by CE Electric.
CE Electric is owned by CalEnergy (rated BB with a stable outlook) and Peter Klewit Sons (unrated).
"The Northern CreditWatch designation acknowledges uncertainties associated with the financial profile and ownership credit exposure of Northern should the bid be sucessful," S&P said in a statement.
Overall, S&P said it believed the acquisition was likely to result in a lower rating on Northern's debt compared to the present level.
"This reflects the potential requirement for Northern to support more debt, as well as the controlling position of BB rated CalEnergy," the agency said.
"At the same time, suitable regulatory ring-fencing provisions in conjunction with other structural features could preserve Northern's rating in the investment grade range," S&P said.
